ENHANCING WATER EFFICIENCY IN SLURRY TRANSPORT SYSTEMS THROUGH A TWO-CHAMBER PNEUMATIC PUMP: DESIGN AND EXPERIMENTAL ANALYSIS

Journal: Water Conservation and Management (WCM)
Author: Yerbol Sarkynov, Yermek Auyelbek, Bauyrzhan Zulpykharov, Darkhan Ordatayev, Algani Aktam and Zhanar Zhakupova

ABSTRACT

This study presents a theoretical model and performance analysis of a novel two-chamber pneumatic pump designed for multiphase slurry transport in shaft wells. The proposed system integrates hydraulic erosion and pneumatic agitation to enhance sediment removal efficiency and ensure continuous operation. A mathematical model describing the operating cycle, pressure requirements, and flow characteristics of the pump is developed based on fluid mechanics and pneumatic transport principles. Key design parameters, including pump head, compressed air pressure, chamber volume, and flow rate, are determined analytically. The results demonstrate that the proposed system provides stable flow conditions and increases productivity by 20–30% compared to conventional single-chamber pumps. The relationship between air pressure and flow rate confirms the effectiveness of the design. The developed model can be used for the design and optimization of pneumatic pumping systems in slurry transport and environmental engineering applications.
